```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
# readModelDb() returns the model *function*; rxode2::rxode() resolves it to
# the rxUi that zeroRe() and the metadata accessors need.
ui_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_venetoclax"))
ui_pk_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui_pk)
ui_er <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_venetoclax_orr"))
```

* Citation: `r ui_pk$reference`
* PK model: `r ui_pk$description`
* Exposure-response model: `r ui_er$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S563629>

Liu and colleagues measured venetoclax trough concentrations in 76 adult
Chinese patients with hematological malignancies, most of them with acute
myeloid leukemia (AML), treated in routine practice at a single Chongqing
centre. Six published venetoclax population PK models, developed mostly in
non-Asian patients, all under-predicted these concentrations, so the authors
fitted a new model: one compartment, first-order absorption with ka fixed at
0.16 1/h (every sample was a trough), CL/F 7.33 L/h and V/F 181 L, with no
covariate retained. In the 63 AML patients they then related the individual
steady-state average concentration (Cave) to the overall response after one
cycle with a univariate logistic regression. The paper packages into two
models here:

* `Liu_2026_venetoclax` -- the population PK model (Table 3).
* `Liu_2026_venetoclax_orr` -- the logistic exposure-response model (Figure
  4B). Its coefficients are not printed and were digitised by the maintainers
  from the fitted curve; the validation is in the exposure-response section
  below.

# Population

```{r population}
str(ui_pk$population)
```

The PK cohort (Table 1) was 76 patients, 46 male and 30 female, median age 53
years (IQR 36-63) and median weight 60 kg (IQR 54-65): AML 63, myelodysplastic
syndrome 7, acute lymphoblastic leukemia 3, and one patient each with acute
promyelocytic leukemia, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia and mixed-phenotype
acute leukemia. Every patient received venetoclax once daily with meals
together with one or two chemotherapy agents, mostly azacitidine; moderate or
strong CYP3A inhibitors and rituximab were exclusion criteria. Patients were
markedly cytopenic at sampling (median platelets 31 x 10^9/L, neutrophils
0.18 x 10^9/L) and most had low albumin. The 63 AML patients of the
exposure-response analysis received 100 mg (n = 7), 200 mg (n = 13), 300 mg
(n = 2) or 400 mg (n = 41) daily (Table S1).

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-compartment, first-order absorption, linear elimination | -- | Results, "VNX PK Characteristics in Chinese Patients" |
| `lka` (ka) | 0.16 1/h, fixed | Table 3 (FIX; from earlier publications, references 36 and 39) |
| `lcl` (CL/F) | 7.33 L/h | Table 3 (RSE 10%) |
| `lvc` (V/F) | 181 L | Table 3 (RSE 30%) |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.53^2) = 0.2475 | Table 3, IIV CL/F 53% CV (shrinkage 6%) |
| `propSd` | 0.32 | Table 3, sigma prop 32% |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` | ng/mL | Analytical Methods (LC-MS/MS in ng/mL); unit conversion only |
| E-R: `logit(p) = logit_ref + e_cav_logit * CAV` | -- | Methods, "Exposure-Efficacy Relationship Evaluation"; Figure 4B |
| `logit_ref` | -0.9055 | Figure 4B fitted curve, digitised (not printed) |
| `e_cav_logit` | 0.0006443 per ng/mL | Figure 4B fitted curve, digitised (not printed; p = 0.0239 printed) |
| `addSd_prob_orr_investigator` | 0.001, fixed | Not from source; placeholder residual for a Bernoulli likelihood |
| `CAV` = daily dose / (24 x CL/F) | ng/mL | Methods, "Exposure-Efficacy Relationship Evaluation" (post hoc PK parameters) |

# Virtual cohort and steady-state simulation

The model has no covariates, so the virtual cohort only needs a dose arm.
Each of the four doses used in the AML subset (100, 200, 300 and 400 mg once
daily) gets 200 subjects, dosed for 14 days (the half-life at the typical
CL/F and V/F is about 17 h, so day 14 is at steady state), with hourly
observations over the last dosing interval.

```{r cohort}
doses <- c(100, 200, 300, 400)
n_per_arm <- 200
tau <- 24
n_doses <- 14
t_ss <- (n_doses - 1) * tau

make_arm <- function(dose, arm_index) {
  ids <- (arm_index - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, t_ss, by = tau)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot")
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = t_ss + 0:tau) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(dose = dose) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) make_arm(doses[i], i)))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261112)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_pk, events = events, keep = "dose", returnType = "data.frame")
# zeroRe() leaves no omega, so rxode2 warns about a multi-subject solve
# without one; that is the intent of a typical-value solve.
sim_typ <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui_pk_typ,
  events = events |> filter(id %in% ((seq_along(doses) - 1) * n_per_arm + 1)),
  keep = "dose", returnType = "data.frame"
))
```

```{r profile-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state venetoclax concentrations over one dosing interval by daily dose (median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 subjects per dose, IIV only), with the typical-value profile dashed. The paper has no concentration-time figure; its samples were all troughs."}
sim |>
  mutate(tad = time - t_ss) |>
  group_by(dose, tad) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(
    data = sim_typ |> mutate(tad = time - t_ss),
    aes(tad, Cc), linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose, "mg QD"), nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Venetoclax (ng/mL)")
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0), tad = time - t_ss, treatment = paste(dose, "mg QD")) |>
  select(id, treatment, tad, Cc)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, time == t_ss) |>
  mutate(tad = 0, treatment = paste(dose, "mg QD")) |>
  select(id, treatment, tad, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ tad | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)

nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "cav")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 4), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin, "Cave (ng/mL)" = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated steady-state NCA parameters by dose (200 subjects per dose).")
```

At steady state Cave equals the daily dose divided by 24 h x CL/F, the
quantity the authors computed from each patient's post hoc CL/F to drive the
exposure-response model. The typical-value solve reproduces that identity, and
the PKNCA Cmin sits close to the 24-h trough because ka (0.16 1/h) is only
four times the elimination rate constant, so the concentration is still
falling when the next dose is given.

```{r closed-form-check}
cl_typ <- exp(ui_pk$theta[["lcl"]])
cav_closed <- 1000 * doses / (tau * cl_typ)
cav_typ_solve <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(
    cav = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) / tau,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Dose (mg)" = doses,
    "Closed form 1000 x dose / (24 x CL/F)" = signif(cav_closed, 4),
    "Typical-value solve (trapezoid)" = signif(cav_typ_solve$cav, 4),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  caption = "Typical steady-state Cave: closed form against the solved typical profile."
)
# Same parameters on both sides; the gap is trapezoid and integrator error
# on an hourly grid, well below 1%.
stopifnot(max(abs(cav_typ_solve$cav / cav_closed - 1)) < 0.01)
```

# Comparison against published exposures

The paper reports two exposure summaries that the model can be held against.
Figure 4B draws a box of the individual post hoc Cave for each daily dose in
the AML patients; the maintainers read the box medians off the publisher's
figure (100, 200, 300 and 400 mg: about 521, 1313, 1938 and 2077 ng/mL). The
Discussion reports a mean observed trough of 1470.18 +/- 855.63 ng/mL in the
200 mg group.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  treatment = paste(doses, "mg QD"),
  cav = c(521, 1313, 1938, 2077)
)
sim_long <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_long,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "cav",
  units = c(cav = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated median steady-state Cave against the Figure 4B per-dose box",
    "medians (digitised). Starred rows differ by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

```{r cmin-200}
cmin200 <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmin", treatment == "200 mg QD")
cmin_tab <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Mean Cmin, 200 mg QD (ng/mL)", "SD (ng/mL)"),
  simulated = signif(c(mean(cmin200$PPORRES), sd(cmin200$PPORRES)), 4),
  published = c(1470.18, 855.63)
)
cmin_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Simulated (IIV only)" = simulated, "Published (observed)" = published) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean steady-state trough at 200 mg once daily: simulation against the observed troughs quoted in the Discussion.")
```

The per-dose Cave medians agree with Figure 4B to within 20% (the
simulated cohort runs high at 100 and 400 mg and low at 200 and 300 mg, where the boxes
hold 7, 41, 13 and 2 patients). The simulated mean trough at 200 mg
(`r sprintf("%.0f", mean(cmin200$PPORRES))` ng/mL) is
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (1 - mean(cmin200$PPORRES) / 1470.18))` lower
than the observed 1470 ng/mL. That observed mean comes from the 200 mg
patients' own troughs, which include the proportional residual error and a
dose group that was not randomised: the Discussion notes that about 40% of
patients on 100-200 mg had relatively high troughs, which is what reduced
doses in routine therapeutic drug monitoring would select for, and the 200 mg
box in Figure 4B already sits above the typical Cave. The model is not tuned
to it.

# Exposure-response model

## Replicating Figure 4B

```{r er-data}
# Individual Cave (ng/mL) of the 63 AML patients, digitised by the maintainers
# from the jittered dot plot of Figure 4A (non-responders left, responders
# right) and cross-checked against the rug circles at p = 0 and p = 1 in
# Figure 4B. Two pairs of responders overlap exactly and are listed twice.
cave_nonresponder <- c(
  328, 381, 540, 553, 699, 723, 1016, 1016, 1110, 1195, 1209, 1231, 1464,
  1509, 1602, 1633, 1813, 1965, 2042, 2074, 2249, 2250, 2705, 3026, 3053, 3812
)
cave_responder <- c(
  515, 699, 885, 911, 1297, 1305, 1318, 1318, 1404, 1514, 1539, 1659, 1675,
  1718, 1731, 1737, 1788, 1822, 2077, 2094, 2172, 2384, 2470, 2470, 2508,
  2517, 2569, 2840, 2934, 2934, 2996, 4421, 4863, 5402, 6192, 6477, 7334
)
er_obs <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(63),
  CAV = c(cave_nonresponder, cave_responder),
  response = rep(0:1, c(length(cave_nonresponder), length(cave_responder)))
)
stopifnot(
  length(cave_nonresponder) == 26, # Results: 26 non-responders
  length(cave_responder) == 37 # Results: 37 responders
)

# Evaluate the packaged model at each patient's Cave. The logistic model has
# no random effect, so rxode2's multi-subject-without-omega warning is
# expected and suppressed in the three solves of this model.
er_pred <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui_er,
  events = er_obs |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 0L),
  keep = c("CAV", "response"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
))
```

```{r er-figure, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4B of Liu 2026: probability of overall response against Cave in the 63 AML patients. The line is the packaged model; squares and bars are the observed response rate and exact 95% CI per Cave quartile, labelled with the counts printed in the figure; ticks mark the individual Cave of non-responders (bottom) and responders (top)."}
q_breaks <- quantile(er_obs$CAV, c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
quart <- er_obs |>
  mutate(q = cut(CAV, q_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(q) |>
  summarise(
    x = median(CAV), n = n(), r = sum(response),
    lo = stats::binom.test(r, n)$conf.int[1],
    hi = stats::binom.test(r, n)$conf.int[2],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(p = r / n, lab = paste0(r, "/", n))

curve <- data.frame(CAV = seq(330, 7350, by = 10)) |>
  mutate(time = 0, evid = 0L, id = seq_len(n()))
curve <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(ui_er, events = curve, keep = "CAV", returnType = "data.frame"))

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = curve, aes(CAV, prob_orr_investigator), colour = "#E07B39", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(data = quart, aes(x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0, colour = "#3C78B4") +
  geom_point(data = quart, aes(x, p), shape = 15, size = 3, colour = "#3C78B4") +
  geom_text(data = quart, aes(x, hi + 0.05, label = lab), colour = "#3C78B4") +
  geom_rug(data = er_obs |> filter(response == 0), aes(CAV), sides = "b") +
  geom_rug(data = er_obs |> filter(response == 1), aes(CAV), sides = "t") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(x = "Cave (ng/mL)", y = "Probability of overall response")
```

## Validating the digitised coefficients

Neither coefficient is printed, so the packaged values come from tracing the
fitted curve in Figure 4B (2283 pixel columns, logit regressed on Cave with
R^2 = 0.99992; against log Cave the fit is visibly worse, R^2 = 0.89, which
settles that Cave enters untransformed). Three checks below use only the
individual Cave values digitised from the other panel (Figure 4A) together
with the printed numbers, not the traced curve:

1. The per-quartile response counts reproduce the four labels printed in
   Figure 4B.
2. A maximum-likelihood logistic refit to the 63 digitised patients
   reproduces the printed AIC (81.81) and p value (0.0239), and its
   coefficients agree with the traced ones.
3. A fitted logistic regression satisfies the score equation exactly: its
   predicted probabilities sum to the number of responders. The packaged
   coefficients, evaluated at the digitised Cave values, must therefore give
   close to 37.

```{r er-validate}
refit <- stats::glm(response ~ CAV, family = stats::binomial(), data = er_obs)
refit_p <- summary(refit)$coefficients["CAV", "Pr(>|z|)"]
loglik_pkg <- sum(stats::dbinom(er_pred$response, 1, er_pred$prob_orr_investigator, log = TRUE))
aic_pkg <- -2 * loglik_pkg + 2 * 2

val <- data.frame(
  check = c(
    "Quartile counts (responders/n)",
    "Intercept",
    "Slope (per ng/mL)",
    "AIC",
    "Wald p for Cave",
    "Sum of predicted probabilities"
  ),
  published = c("4/16, 12/16, 9/15, 12/16", "not printed", "not printed", "81.81", "0.0239", "37 responders"),
  packaged_model = c(
    "--",
    sprintf("%.4f", ui_er$theta[["logit_ref"]]),
    sprintf("%.3e", ui_er$theta[["e_cav_logit"]]),
    sprintf("%.2f", aic_pkg),
    "--",
    sprintf("%.2f", sum(er_pred$prob_orr_investigator))
  ),
  refit_to_digitised_patients = c(
    paste(quart$lab, collapse = ", "),
    sprintf("%.4f", coef(refit)[[1]]),
    sprintf("%.3e", coef(refit)[[2]]),
    sprintf("%.2f", stats::AIC(refit)),
    sprintf("%.4f", refit_p),
    sprintf("%.2f", sum(stats::fitted(refit)))
  )
)
val |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Check" = check, "Published" = published,
    "Packaged (traced curve)" = packaged_model,
    "Refit to digitised Figure 4A" = refit_to_digitised_patients
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Digitised exposure-response coefficients against the numbers printed in Figure 4.")

stopifnot(
  identical(quart$lab, c("4/16", "12/16", "9/15", "12/16")),
  abs(stats::AIC(refit) - 81.81) < 0.05,
  abs(refit_p - 0.0239) < 0.0005,
  abs(aic_pkg - 81.81) < 0.05,
  abs(sum(er_pred$prob_orr_investigator) - 37) < 0.5,
  abs(coef(refit)[[2]] / ui_er$theta[["e_cav_logit"]] - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The traced curve and the refit agree to within 1% on the slope and 0.004 on
the intercept, and the packaged coefficients reproduce the printed AIC to
the second decimal. The Wilcoxon comparison in Figure 4A (p = 0.012) is also
reproduced by the digitised values:
`r sprintf("p = %.4f", suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(cave_responder, cave_nonresponder))$p.value)`.

## Predicted response by dose

Chaining the two models -- each simulated subject's steady-state Cave from the
PK cohort fed into the logistic model -- gives the model-implied response
rate per dose. This is a property of the fitted curve, not a reproduction of
a published table; the paper describes the observed response rate rising from
about 42% at 100 mg to 68% at 200 mg in small, non-randomised dose groups.

```{r er-by-dose}
cav_sim <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  transmute(id, treatment, CAV = PPORRES, time = 0, evid = 0L)
orr_sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(ui_er, events = cav_sim, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"))
orr_sim |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    median_cav = signif(median(CAV), 4),
    mean_prob = round(mean(prob_orr_investigator), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment, "Median Cave (ng/mL)" = median_cav,
    "Model-predicted response rate" = mean_prob
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model-implied overall response rate by dose from the chained PK and exposure-response models (200 simulated subjects per dose).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 3 gives the between-subject variability on CL/F as
  "53%" under the heading CV%. It is encoded as a log-normal variance
  `log(1 + 0.53^2) = 0.2475`. If the authors' 53% is instead the square root
  of the NONMEM omega, the variance would be 0.2809; the two readings differ
  by about 3 percentage points in CV.
* **ka fixed.** ka = 0.16 1/h is the value the authors fixed from earlier
  venetoclax models because every sample was a trough. Absorption-phase
  concentrations, Cmax and Tmax from this model are therefore not informed
  by the Chinese data.
* **No covariates.** The stepwise search found none. The screened
  demographic and laboratory covariates are listed in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Exposure-response coefficients digitised.** `logit_ref` and
  `e_cav_logit` were traced from Figure 4B of the publisher's PDF; the
  validation above reproduces the printed AIC, p value and quartile counts.
  The individual Cave values in this vignette were digitised from Figure 4A
  and are approximate to a few ng/mL.
* **Response definition.** "Overall response" here is complete or partial
  remission on the bone-marrow assessment after one 28-day cycle, judged by
  the treating physician against Chinese adult-AML guideline criteria; it
  has no separate category for complete remission with incomplete count
  recovery and is not a RECIST response.
* **Placeholder residual.** The logistic model carries a fixed additive
  residual of 0.001 on the probability so that it has an error model; the
  source likelihood is Bernoulli.
* **Analyses not packaged.** The same logistic analysis with Cmin as the
  exposure metric in the AML subset (Figure S7) and the sensitivity analyses
  in all 76 patients (Figures S8 and S9) are not encoded; Cave in the AML
  subset is the primary analysis the authors carried forward.
* **Cohort.** The simulations use 200 subjects per dose with no covariate
  dependence; the published dose groups were small (7, 13, 2 and 41 AML
  patients) and not randomised.
